newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes lower but TWI hits 8-1/2 yr high.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes lower but TWI hits 8-1/2 yr high.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed weaker on Friday after its spectacular rise on Thursday and overnight.
Dealers said the Kiwi was following the Australian dollar, which had rallied strongly on Thursday only to relinquish much of its gain this session.

Kiwi closed at US$0.6925/32, down from 0.6940/45 at its local open. It had traded a wide 0.6910-75 range last night, its Trade-Weighted Index hitting an 8-1/2 year high of 69.16. The TWI closed at 68.98.
"Considering the movement overnight, it's been a reasonably quite day. We've really just come off into the mid-0.6920s with the Aussie backing off all day," said a chief back dealer.

"There's been a little bit of selling out of Hong Kong this afternoon, which pushed it back to the 0.6930/35 level. It looks like it could trade back to the 0.6910 level if the Aussie trades a little bit lower," he said.
Dealers said Kiwi was finding support around 69 figure 10.
"Really Kiwi's almost just been following the Aussie dollar. If the Aussie trades back below US$0.7630, that means that this move up has just been a correction," said the chief dealer.
The Aussie was at US$0.7635/40 at the New Zealand close.
Dealers said that if the New Zealand dollar didn't trade above 0.6950 early next week, that would confirm the downtrend.
